In [[geometry]], the '''gyroelongated pentagonal cupolarotunda''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|47}}}}). As the name suggests, it can be constructed by gyroelongating a pentagonal cupolarotunda ({{math|[[pentagonal orthocupolarotunda|''J''{{sub|32}}]]}} or {{math|[[pentagonal gyrocupolarotunda|''J''{{sub|33}}]]}}) by inserting a [[decagon]]al [[antiprism]] between its two halves.

{{Johnson solid}}

The gyroelongated pentagonal cupolarotunda is one of five Johnson solids which are [[chirality (mathematics)|chiral]], meaning that they have a "left-handed" and a "right-handed" form. In the illustration to the right, each pentagonal face on the bottom half of the figure is connected by a path of two triangular faces to a square face above it and to the left. In the figure of opposite chirality (the mirror image of the illustrated figure), each bottom pentagon would be connected to a square face above it and to the right. The two chiral forms of {{math|''J''{{sub|47}}}} are not considered different Johnson solids.
[[File:J47 gyroelongated pentagonal cupolarotunda.stl|thumb|3D model of a gyroelongated pentagonal cupolarotunda]]

== Area and volume ==
With edge length a, the surface area is

:<math>A=\frac{1}{4}\left(20+35\sqrt{3}+7\sqrt{25+10\sqrt{5}}\right)a^2\approx32.198786370...a^2,</math>

and the volume is

:<math>V=\left(\frac{55}{12}+\frac{25}{12}\sqrt{5}+ \frac{5}{6}\sqrt{2\sqrt{650+290\sqrt{5}}-2\sqrt{5}-2}\right) a^3</math> <math>\approx15.991096162...a^3.</math>
